chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from some of our companions, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When the death came upon al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him), he said: 'O Qanbar! Look around — do you see from behind your door a believer from other than the progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him)?' He replied: 'God the Exalted, His Messenger, and the son of His Messenger know better than I.' He said: 'Call Muhammad ibn Ali for me.' So I (Qanbar) went to him, and when I entered upon him, he said: 'Has anything happened except good?' I said: 'Respond to Abu Muhammad.' So he hastened with his sandal strap without straightening it, and went out with me running. When he stood before him, he greeted. Al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Sit down, for one such as you should not be absent from hearing a speech by which the dead are revived and the living can die. Be receptacles of knowledge and lanterns of guidance, for the light of the day — part of it is more luminous than other parts.

Do you not know that God made the children of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) Imams and gave distinction to some of them over others, and gave the Psalms to Dawud (peace be upon him)? And you know what He chose to distinguish Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) with. O Muhammad ibn Ali! I fear envy for you, for God has described the disbelievers with it, and God Almighty said: [2:109] unbelievers, out of envy from themselves, even after the truth became clear to them. And God Almighty will not give Satan authority over you. O Muhammad ibn Ali! Shall I tell you what I heard from your father regarding you?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'I heard your father (peace be upon him) saying on the day of Basra: Whoever loves to honor me in this world and the next, let him honor Muhammad, my son.

O Muhammad ibn Ali! If I wished, I could have informed you while you were still a drop of seed in your father's loins! O Muhammad ibn Ali! Do you not know that al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), after my passing and the departure of my soul from my body, will be the Imam after me? And before God — Majestic is His Name — it is in the Book as an inheritance from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), which God Almighty has assigned to him in the inheritance of his father and his mother. God knew that you are the best of His creation, and He chose Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) from among you, and Muhammad chose Ali (peace be upon him), and Ali (peace be upon him) chose me for the Imamate, and I hereby choose al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'

Muhammad ibn Ali said to him: 'You are an Imam and you are my means to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). By God, I would have wished that my soul had departed before I heard this speech from you. Indeed, in my head there are words that neither can buckets drain nor can the songs of the winds alter — like a lexicon book in decorated pages. I intend to express them and find that I have been preceded to it — preceded by the Revealed Book or what the Messengers came with. It is a speech that exhausts the tongues of speakers and the hands of writers, until no pen is found and paper is brought as ashes, yet it cannot reach your virtues. And thus does God reward the doers of good, and there is no power except with God.

Al-Husayn is the most knowledgeable of us in knowledge, the most forbearing of us in clemency, and the closest of us to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) in kinship. He was a jurist before he was created, and he read the Revelation before he spoke. And had God known any goodness in anyone else, He would not have chosen Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). So when God chose Muhammad, and Muhammad chose Ali, and Ali chose you as Imam, and you chose al-Husayn — we submit and we are pleased. Who is there who would be pleased with other than him? And with whom other than him could we be safe from the difficulties of our affairs?'

key_terms.أَوْعِيَةَ الْعِلْمِ: Receptacles/vessels of knowledge — those who preserve and carry divine knowledge
key_terms.الْإِمَامَة: The Imamate — divine leadership of the Muslim community after the Prophet
key_terms.الْحَسَد: Envy — Imam Hasan warns Muhammad ibn Ali against this trait which characterized the disbelievers
key_terms.مَصَابِيحَ الْهُدَى: Lanterns of guidance — those who illuminate the path for others
key_terms.وِرَاثَة: Inheritance — used here in the theological sense of divinely ordained succession

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Hasan designate Imam Husayn as the next Imam before his death?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a momentous deathbed scene: Imam Hasan (AS), approaching death, summons his half-brother Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya (Muhammad ibn Ali) to formally designate Imam Husayn (AS) as the next Imam. The narrative unfolds in Medina, shortly before the death of Imam Hasan (AS) in 50 AH. The hadith establishes the principle of divine selection through a chain: God chose Muhammad, Muhammad chose Ali, Ali chose Hasan, and Hasan chose Husayn — a foundational doctrine in Shia theology of the Imamate. Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya's eloquent response acknowledges Husayn's unparalleled virtues, affirming his submission and acceptance.
